key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon sink substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a sustainable reactor/material strategy for improving photocatalytic carbon conversion by pairing catalyst design with biologically sourced sacrificial agents.
method: Designed an AB2O6 high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered-perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs/Ba to increase surface basicity, Bi to promote polarization and charge separation, and Nb/Ta to support charge transport.
Compared CO2 photocatalysis with no sacrificial agent, with microplastics, and with microalgae as the sacrificial agent.
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on maintaining microalgae stability, light access, and scalable separation/handling of biomass in a real photocatalytic reactor.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
